lead: Strategy / MSTR — the copycats move into bitcoin
smaller: Ether / ETH — the network is busy, the price is not
Advanced Micro Devices / AMD — the 10x Radeon claim
Tesla / TSLA — the comeback still rests on Musk
why_lead: The draft lead (Tesla, Musk back in charge) repeated the all-hands 'hang on' and tariff-leeway catalysts that already led on 24 and 25 March; the new 25 March items are attention headlines and a larger five-session move, not a new catalyst, so Tesla is kept only as a shortened smaller carryover. Strategy is the strongest bitcoin proxy (five-session +20.70%, 20-session +36.45%) and its catalysts are new: GameStop's 25 March plan to invest corporate cash in bitcoin, Metaplanet's 150-bitcoin addition (24 March) and the 25 March preferred-stock comparisons, while bitcoin is down 3.48% over 20 sessions. The 25 March smaller covered 'Saylor buys again', so this is a changed story, not a repeat.
why_smaller: Ether / ETH: the network-versus-price story is new. Its inputs are a 20 March stablecoin-volume headline, 21 March lag explainers and a 24 March CoinShares report that XRP and Solana lead altcoin ETP inflows as Ethereum slumps; the ether fund is down 16.52% over 20 sessions. Solana was used on 24 March, but for the ETF and cabal items, not for ether.

Advanced Micro Devices / AMD: the 10x Radeon claim (25 March, two headlines) is the crowd's number, and its first-week caveat is the break. AMD is up 10.44% over 20 sessions while the semiconductor ETF is down 4.68%, so the rebound is stock-specific; AMD had no smaller or lead trade earlier in this series.

Tesla / TSLA: a shortened carryover because the catalysts (tariff leeway, all-hands call) are unchanged; the new items are the 25 March attention headlines and the Europe sales headlines that cut against the rebound.
considered_not_chosen: Tesla as the lead again: a fourth Tesla lead in about two weeks on the same tariff and all-hands catalysts; the 25 March headlines are attention, not a new catalyst.
GameStop / GME as its own lead: the copycat pop is the lead's catalyst, and the market move is modest (five-session +9.01%, 20-session +4.01%).
Alibaba / BABA (chairman's AI-bubble warning, 25 March; five-session -7.00%): the warning already appears in the sectors and catalysts sections of this edition, so retail does not repeat it.
Solana / SOL: the 24 March smaller already used the Bloomberg memecoin-cabal item and the 2x Solana ETF buzz headline.
Quantum / QBTS: the Nvidia Quantum Day and skeptic catalysts ran on 19 and 21 March; the 25 March buy-the-dip headline adds no new catalyst.
Robinhood / HOOD: the Massachusetts probe was the 25 March smaller.
Leveraged ETFs / TQQQ: the 21 March smaller and the flows section already cover the free fall.
Silver / SLV and gold: the gold family ran as smaller trades on 17, 19 and 24 March.
Carvana / CVNA (five-session +33.11%): trade-press headlines only, no retail-attention evidence.
Krispy Kreme, MicroAlgo, United Airlines, CoreWeave: retail-attention headlines but no market-data price, so they cannot be priced.
Novo Nordisk and Oklo: covered in the sectors and Europe sections, with media rather than retail attention.
Hims & Hers: a five-session +17.62% with no retail headline in the window.
